subject: ventures/patio-door-bid-calculator
professional: a window and door installation contractor who bids sliding / patio-door replacements; first checks: does changing the unit (panels, frame, glass) and the install method move the price, is labor loaded with burden, is margin taken on price not cost, is the walk-away the true cost, is a crew of two priced as two people's hours, and are new-construction flashing / sill pan hours counted once

evidence.correctness: Engine arithmetic recomputed by hand and run (`node /tmp/claude-0/audit-patio/calc-cases.mjs`). Defaults: hours 1 + 4.5 + 1.4 tear-out + 0.5 site = 7.4; loaded wage 48 x 1.32 = 63.36; labor 468.864; material 980 + 65 dump = 1045; travel 110; direct 1623.864; overhead 16% 259.818; cost 1883.68; price 1883.68/0.68 = 2770.12: match. Heavy preset (16-ft 4-panel fiberglass impact new-con balcony, all extras): set (11.5+0.55+0.7) x 1.35 = 17.2125 h, total 32.6125 h, door 2100 x 3.05 x 1.65 = 10568.25, cost 15874.11, price 23344.28: match. Own case (9-ft 3-panel aluminum triple retrofit balcony, screen + sill pan, no tear-out, $40 wage, 25% burden, 10% OH, 25% margin, $150 travel, $120 permit): 13.5 h, labor 675, door 1420 x 1.75 x 1.28 = 3180.80, cost 4824.38, price 6432.51; proposed $6,000 -> profit 1175.62, margin 19.59%: match. Not a 3, because what the page shows is wrong in common use: I drove index.html's own module script with a minimal fake DOM (`node /tmp/claude-0/audit-patio/page-cases.mjs`; no jsdom in the container). The page saves the whole form on load (index.html:697) and on the next visit restores it and marks every field hand-edited (index.html:627), so the configuration, frame, glazing, install and access selects stop updating the rates: on a second visit, switching to 16-ft 4-panel, wood-clad, impact, new-construction, balcony still prices $2,770.12 (the 6-ft vinyl price; first visit gives $6,953.83 for the config change alone). Blank fields price silently: blank wage -> $1,970.29 (labor 0), blank margin -> $1,883.68 at $0 profit, '1,200' typed in the unit cost (a type=number input yields '') -> $1,098.36 with no door cost, no error.
evidence.completeness: Checked against README and page: config/frame/glazing/install/access kits (work on a first visit only, see correctness), six extras toggles (work), loaded labor (works), margin-on-price (works), walk-away and proposed-price verdict (works: $1,800 -> 'loses $83.68', walk-away $1,883.68), hour and cost split (works), Copy bid summary without wages (formatBidSummary read, tests pass), saved bid and bid link (share.test.mjs passes, restore works, but it disables the kits), printable proposal (proposal.test.mjs passes; refresh logic read index.html:821-840), usage opt-out with DNT/GPC (usage.test.mjs). Three guide/comparison pages present, linked and in the sitemap. No TODOs or stubs. The kit behaviour is the core feature the page sells ('Changing configuration ... never overwrites a rate you already typed'), and after the first visit it does nothing for rates nobody typed.
evidence.verification: `cd ventures/patio-door-bid-calculator && node --test '*.test.mjs'`: 143 tests, 143 pass, 259 ms. Seven seeded mutants with platform/ci/quality_mutate.py: calc.mjs set-hour factor dropped (caught), margin as markup (caught), hourly rate excluding materials (caught), dump fee not gated on tear-out (caught), belowBreakEven < -> <= (survived, boundary only); index.html applyKit never applying non-forced kits (SURVIVED) and readInput falling back to defaultValue for blanks (SURVIVED). The engine is well guarded; the page logic that decides which numbers reach the engine has no behavioural test at all (page.test.mjs is regex over the HTML), which is where the high defect lives.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (426 lines), index.html module script (index.html:334-886), share.mjs restore/save, the vs-a-flat test. Engine: pure, validated selects, strict yes/no flags, finite checks. Defects: applyValues marks every restored field edited (index.html:621-629), interacting with the unconditional persist() at load (index.html:697) so the kit 'edited' state is lost on every revisit; the same block is in 36 venture index.html files; number() accepts '' as 0 (calc.mjs:118); applyKit carries a dead `ids` branch (index.html:393-395); the money formatter is duplicated between calc.mjs:393 and index.html:371.
evidence.claims: Checked: disclaimer in index footer, README and guide pages (present); 'Nothing is uploaded' (no fetch in the page script; served extra modules pf-rates/pf-jobs say local-only); guide page figures $2,770.12, $1,883.68, $23,344.28, $15,874.11, $83.68 (all reproduced); served page https://marisstella.app/patio-door-bid-calculator/ returns 200 with canonical on marisstella.app, llms.txt origins marisstella.app and github.com. Not backed: vs-a-flat-installed-price.html:74-79 and its FAQ JSON-LD (line 12) label the bid price at a 32% margin as the 'Walk-away price' and say the $1,800 special 'Loses $970.12' on the brochure hang, $6,175.38 and $21,544.28 on the others; the tool's own walk-away is total cost ($1,883.68) and its own verdict at $1,800 is 'loses $83.68' (losses vs cost on the other two are $3,623.66 and $14,074.11), so the page contradicts the calculator and the guide page; README.md:84-85 lists 4 counted events, the page records 7 (also link_copied, proposal_printed, company_forgotten); README.md:57 calls price/hours an 'effective hourly billing rate' and the verdict says 'billing $X/h of labor' (index.html:518) while the figure includes the door and all material ($374.34/h on defaults, labor-only $63.36 loaded cost).
evidence.fitness: Walked the job: a shop prices a 6-ft vinyl retrofit, then the next day opens the page to price a 12-ft 3-panel new-construction unit. Picking the new configuration, glass and install method changes the labels and the summary scope but not the hours or unit cost, and the bid summary / printed proposal would carry '12-foot 3-panel ... New-construction' at the 6-ft price unless the shop notices and applies a job preset or types each rate. Within a first visit the tool does the job in a few minutes. Crew size is not modelled: hours are 'crew-hours' at one wage (calc.mjs:417), so a two-person set of a 16-ft impact unit must be entered as doubled hours, which nothing on the page says. No line for stucco/siding cut-back, header or rough-opening change, or glass disposal weight; the README states one-opening and no-tax limits.
evidence.domain: Compared against how an installer builds a patio-door bid (unit cost from the supplier quote by size/panel count/glass, crew-hours by person, burden on wage, flashing per ASTM E2112 / manufacturer instructions with a sill pan as part of the new-construction install, material markup often set apart from labor margin). Matches: loaded wage, margin as share of price, walk-away = cost, impact glazing flagged as a code question. Departs: the new-construction kit's wrap hours are described as covering 'flashing, sill pan, and exterior wrap' (calc.mjs:193-195) yet the new-con presets also tick the separate sill-pan extra (calc.mjs:97, :111: +1.5 h and +$165), so the pan is counted twice; overhead and full margin are applied to a $10,568 door unit the same as to labor, which is a choice a door shop usually makes separately; crew-hours at one wage; starting rates uncited (stated as ballpark).

verdict: Below the bar. The engine is right: three hand-computed bids (the default retrofit, the heavy 4-panel impact balcony preset and an independent 3-panel aluminum case) and every figure on the guide page reproduce to the cent, 143 tests pass and four of five engine mutants are caught. But the page that feeds the engine breaks its central feature on every return visit: because the form is saved on load and every restored field is marked hand-edited, changing the configuration, frame, glass, install method or access stops moving the price, so a 16-ft 4-panel impact new-construction balcony door is quoted at the 6-ft vinyl $2,770.12 (shown by driving index.html's own script). Blank or comma-typed fields silently price as zero, the comparison page calls the marked-up price the 'walk-away' and overstates the $1,800 special's loss ($970.12 vs the tool's own $83.68), and new-construction presets count the sill pan twice. No page-level test exists, so none of this is caught. Correctness, claims and verification are each 2.
